name: Kamikaze
description: Kamikaze is a half-pipe tube slide where two riders sit facing each other in a double tube and swing from side to side as they drop down the slide. Opened in 2008, it can run wet or dry and is one of the park's most talked-about thrill rides. Riders must be taller than 110 cm and stay within the combined weight limit of 180 kg.

name: Tornado
description: Tornado is a ProSlide funnel slide that opened in 2006 as part of the Extreme H2O Zone. Four riders share a clover-leaf raft and drop into a giant funnel, swirling up and down its walls at up to 40 km/h before shooting out of the bottom. It is a favourite for groups because everyone rides together.

name: Zoom Zone
description: Zoom Zone is the park's newest slide complex, opened in December 2025 on the site of the former AquaLoop. Four enclosed WhiteWater AquaTube body slides leave from a tower about 17.6 m high, with colourful lighting effects inside. The teal and orange Twisters are the gentler pair, while the dark blue and yellow Loopers are more intense, with big helices. All four slides share one queue, where lifeguards measure riders: Twisters from 102 cm, Loopers from 120 cm.

name: Super Ripper
description: Super Ripper is a pair of body slides that race side by side down short, twisty tracks, built by WhiteWater West as the Southern Hemisphere's first Parallel Pursuit. It opened in December 2021 in the same tower as Kaboom! and Double Barrel. Lie back, go head to head with a friend and see who reaches the bottom first.

name: Kaboom!
description: Kaboom! is Wet'n'Wild's dueling Master Blaster with Tailspin Fusion, built by WhiteWater West and opened in December 2021. From a 27 m tower, riders in tubes drop down two mirrored slides, then are blasted uphill by fast jets of water before spinning through a high-banked Tailspin section. Reported to be the tallest water slide in Australia, it is the park's headline thrill. Check the official site for the height rules.

name: Blackhole
description: Blackhole is a pair of enclosed tube slides that opened in 2006 as part of the Extreme H2O Zone. Riders sit in a tube and plunge into the dark, twisting and turning through the tunnel until they splash out at the bottom. It is a great pick for guests who like the thrill of not knowing what comes next.

name: Mammoth Falls
description: Mammoth Falls is a pair of raft slides where up to six riders share a large inflatable raft. Opened in 2000 and rebuilt in 2005 as a mirror image of the original, it takes the whole group on a splashy trip through dips and turns, and is ideal for families and friend groups. Kids need to be at least 100 cm tall, and each raft has a maximum total weight of 660 kg.

name: Giant Wave Pool
description: The Giant Wave Pool has been part of Wet'n'Wild since the park opened in 1984, and was Australia's first wave pool. Holding about 3 million litres of water, it produces swells of around a metre, giving guests an ocean-style experience without leaving the park. A classic spot to float, swim and cool off between slides.

name: H2Oasis
description: H2Oasis is a zero-depth splash zone built next to the park's biggest slides, described when it was announced as the largest zero-depth water play area on the Gold Coast. It has fountains, props and shaded seating for parents, making it an easy, safe place for young children to splash while older family members ride the slides.

name: Wet'n'Wild Junior
description: Wet'n'Wild Junior is the children's area of the park, refurbished in 2014. It has a WhiteWater play structure and a set of ProSlide Junior Slides, including funnel, wide and racing slides sized for little guests. A safe and fun place for toddlers and young children to splash, climb and slide with their parents nearby.

name: Calypso Beach Lazy River
description: Calypso Beach is Wet'n'Wild's lazy river, a tropical, beach-style setting where you hop into a single tube and let the gentle current carry you around. It is the calm break between the big slides, perfect for resting your legs, chatting with friends or giving younger children a relaxed way to enjoy the water.
